headline: 790 hospitalised in 24 hours as dengue claims 2 more lives
summary: The total death toll from dengue has risen to 141, with nearly 50,000 cases reported across Bangladesh.
details: At least two dengue patients died and 790 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services.
One death was reported from Dhaka North City Corporation and the other from the Chattogram division.
With these latest additions, the total number of dengue cases in the country has reached 49,220.
The overall death toll from the virus has now risen to 141.
Currently, 3,434 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals nationwide.

topic: 63 foreigners arrested for alleged illegal activities
headline_marked: 63 foreigners [[detained in Chattogram for online fraud]]
headline: 63 foreigners detained in Chattogram for online fraud
summary: Police raided an 8-story building in the Jalalabad residential area, uncovering a network using servers and computers to scam people globally.
details: Police arrested 63 foreign nationals from 14 flats in an 8-story building in the Jalalabad residential area of Khulshi, Chattogram. The suspects, including 34 from Laos, 21 from Pakistan, 5 from China, 2 and from Nepal, and 1 from Vietnam, had been operating there for about a month and a half.

Authorities recovered 170 electronic devices, including laptops, mobile phones, and servers. According to Additional Commissioner Faisal Ahmed, the group had established an online fraud network, using fake websites and job offers to steal money from victims.

The foreigners did not have their passports or visas with them; these documents were held by a local syndicate that helped them rent the building and set up the operation. Police are currently working to identify and arrest the members of this local ring.
Preliminary investigations suggest the group moved to Bangladesh after crackdowns on online scams in Laos, Vietnam, and Cambodia made it difficult to operate in those countries.
Police are also investigating whether this operation is linked to a similar raid in Cox's Bazar on September 3, where six foreigners were arrested and nearly 2,000 iPhones were seized from a hotel.

The 63 detainees have been sent to jail and a case has been filed under the Cyber Security Act. Police will seek remand for further interrogation to uncover the full extent of the network and the amount of money stolen.
caption:
63 foreigners from 5 different countries arrested in a single building in Chattogram. They were running a massive online scam network.

Police arrested 63 foreign nationals from 14 flats in an 8-story building in the Jalalabad residential area of Khulshi, Chattogram. The suspects, including 34 from Laos, 21 from Pakistan, 5 from China, 2 and from Nepal, and 1 from Vietnam, had been operating there for about a month and a half.

Authorities recovered 170 electronic devices, including laptops, mobile phones, and servers. According to Additional Commissioner Faisal Ahmed, the group had established an online fraud network, using fake websites and job offers to steal money from victims.

The foreigners did not have their passports or visas with them; these documents were held by a local syndicate that helped them rent the building and set up the operation. Police are currently working to identify and arrest the members of this local ring.

Preliminary investigations suggest the group moved to Bangladesh after crackdowns on online scams in Laos, Vietnam, and Cambodia made it difficult to operate in those countries.

Police are also investigating whether this operation is linked to a similar raid in Cox's Bazar on September 3, where six foreigners were arrested and nearly 2,000 iPhones were seized from a hotel.

The 63 detainees have been sent to jail and a case has been filed under the Cyber Security Act. Police will seek remand for further interrogation to uncover the full extent of the network and the amount of money stolen.
